education.title: Education — Ground Reality
education.source_note: UDISE+ 2023-24 / 2024-25 reports, Ministry of Education; Economic Survey 2024-25 (via PIB)
ground_reality: 1,10,971 schools across India have only a single teacher, serving nearly 40 lakh students between them — an average of 36 students per teacher in these specific schools, per UDISE+ 2023-24.

12,964 schools reported zero enrolled students in 2023-24, while still employing 31,981 teachers between them — a real, sourced anomaly worth investigating at the state level (Madhya Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh account for the largest numbers of single-teacher schools).
Pupil-teacher ratios have genuinely improved at every level since 2014-15 and are now better than NEP 2020's recommended 1:30 standard across the board.

This dashboard does not yet have state-wise or district-wise school/teacher data ingested — the national picture above is real, but a true 'ground reality vs budget' comparison needs per-district figures cross-referenced with local education budget allocations, which is a follow-up ingestion task.

environment.title: Environment — Paris Agreement & Forest Fund Tracking
environment.source_note: Climate Action Tracker; PRS/CBGA budget analyses; India's NDC filings under UNFCCC

ndc_targets.status: Achieved in 2024 — 5 years early (242.78 GW, ~50% of 484.82 GW total)

ndc_targets.goal: 2.5–3 billion tonnes CO2-equivalent via forest/tree cover by 2030
ndc_targets.status: Progress not independently confirmed in sources checked for this update

ground_reality: CAMPA (Compensatory Afforestation Fund) utilisation remains poor — states are spending only a fraction of released funds, per independent climate-policy analysis. This matches the CAG findings already on this dashboard's Deforestation topic (e.g. the Uttarakhand case, where CAMPA funds were found diverted to non-forestry purchases).
India met its 50% non-fossil power capacity target five years ahead of the 2030 deadline — a genuinely verified, positive figure, not just a promise.

The forest carbon sink target (2.5–3 billion tonnes CO2-equivalent) does not have a clear, independently confirmed current progress figure in the sources checked here — flagged as a gap rather than estimated.
India missed the February 2025 deadline to submit updated 2035 NDC targets, a fact independently reported but with no single official explanation found in sources checked.
